projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The synchronized drop of 6 connected devices between 08:15–08:31, followed by stabilization at ~20–21 devices with zero camera motion, confirms a quiet, routine Tuesday morning departure for school and work. The absence of camera alerts alongside the stable device count indicates a normal, non-emergency exit pattern.

The steady decline of 6 connected devices between 08:15–08:31, combined with zero camera activity, indicates a staggered family departure for school/work via the garage. The subsequent stabilization at 20 devices suggests a consistent baseline, likely one adult home or persistent IoT.

The steady decline in connected devices from 26 to 20 between 08:15 and 08:31, paired with zero camera activity, confirms a coordinated morning departure for school and work rather than a network glitch or security event.

The sustained presence count of 25-28 devices during deep night hours, paired with zero camera activity and prior sleep tracker anomalies, confirms that UniFi presence detection is miscounting IoT devices and wearables as mobile phones rather than indicating actual human presence or guests. This is a known sensor artifact, but monitoring it prevents false security alerts.

The fluctuating presence count of 25-28 devices at 4 AM, paired with the sleep tracker anomaly and zero camera activity, indicates the system is counting connected IoT/wearables or stale connections rather than human movement, confirming all occupants are asleep and preventing false nighttime alerts.

Sleep trackers reported ~12 hours of sleep at 00:21, indicating stale data or that the trackers were removed, which means current sleep quality metrics are unreliable. The home is otherwise in a normal overnight state with no activity or security concerns.

The sustained 24–27 connected devices alongside zero camera motion suggests the household is likely gathered in a single area (e.g., watching a movie or gaming) or experiencing a network reporting anomaly; a quick camera status check is recommended to ensure all feeds are active.

The sustained 24–27 device count paired with zero camera motion strongly indicates Wi-Fi presence detection is counting smart home IoT devices rather than people, suggesting the family is likely in an unmonitored area or network presence settings need tuning.

The sustained 24–27 mobile device count alongside zero camera motion over two hours strongly indicates the security cameras are offline or malfunctioning, rather than a normal quiet evening. This matters because it leaves the home unmonitored during prime family hours.

The sustained 20–25 device count alongside zero camera activity on a Monday evening strongly suggests a guest gathering or family event, but warrants a quick check to ensure cameras are online and not in low-light standby mode.
